chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nuflī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The divorce of the mute woman is that he takes her head-covering and places it on her head, then he separates from her.
ai.seo_question: How is a divorce legally executed for a mute woman according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s chain in al-Istibsar establishes a pragmatic legal mechanism for divorcing a mute woman, addressing the absence of verbal consent or declaration in Shia fiqh. By utilizing the physical removal and placement of the miqna'ah (a specific head covering), the husband creates a tangible, observable sign of separation that serves as valid evidence of the divorce, ensuring clarity in marital status without requiring speech.
